purpose: Assesses whether the organization allocates and documents AI-related responsibilities across its supply chain, including AI vendors, service providers, and customers who consume its AI systems.
summary: This objective requires the organization to manage AI-related risks that arise from third-party relationships, including allocating responsibility across the AI supply chain, understanding how third-party AI components (models, data, tooling) affect the organization's own AI systems, and clarifying obligations toward customers who use or are affected by the organization's AI systems.
expectedStatementElements: How AI-related responsibilities are allocated and documented between the organization and its AI vendors/suppliers
What due diligence is performed on third-party AI components (models, datasets, platforms) before integration
How the organization communicates AI-related obligations, limitations, and support terms to customers
How supply chain risk (e.g., a vendor's AI system being compromised or discontinued) is monitored and mitigated
evidenceExamples: Contracts or agreements documenting AI-related responsibility allocation with vendors and suppliers
Due diligence records/questionnaires completed for third-party AI components before integration
Customer-facing terms of service or documentation covering AI-related obligations and limitations
Supply chain risk register covering third-party AI dependencies
commonGaps: Contracts with AI vendors don't clearly allocate responsibility for AI-related risks or incidents
Third-party models or datasets are integrated without any documented due diligence process
Customers aren't clearly informed about the AI-related obligations or limitations that apply to them
No visibility exists into what happens if a key AI vendor is compromised or discontinues a critical service
interviewQuestions: If an AI vendor's model caused a problem, would our contract make clear who's responsible?
Before integrating a third-party model or dataset, do we do any kind of due diligence on it?
Do our customers know what AI-related obligations or limitations apply to them?
If a critical AI vendor got compromised or shut down tomorrow, would we know our exposure?
